decision.argument_basis: scope evidence not reflected in the mapping
decision.evidence_cited: Employee "built and owns the branch predictor sizing model for the NX-500 core, which directly set the BTB capacity used in the final tapeout" and required only "light-touch" review compared to a typical new grad. Per Nyx's own anchors (section 4), this is full, unsupervised ownership of a tapeout-scale piece of work with reduced oversight -- the defining indicator of MTS II ("Owns a component or sub-block independently, start to finish; makes routine technical judgment calls without asking... Full, unsupervised ownership of at least one tapeout-scale piece of work"), not MTS I ("Works within an established area under a more senior engineer's direction; contributes a defined piece of a larger block rather than owning one outright... supervised sign-off"). The role summary describes ownership and lightened supervision, not a defined sub-piece under direction. The proposed L3 mapping appears calibrated to the MTS I label on record rather than to this described scope, and section 3 is explicit that title/level labels are the record of a past decision, not evidence for a new one.
decision.framework_section: Section 4 (Level anchors: MTS I vs. MTS II) and Section 3 (Leveling principle -- title is not self-executing)
